quiz.question: What happens to ordinary TypeScript type annotations and interfaces when TypeScript is compiled/transpiled to JavaScript?
options: They are converted into automatic runtime API validators
They are erased (type erasure) before browser execution, so runtime validation is still required for external API data
They are stored in LocalStorage
They run inside a Web Worker
quiz.explanation: Type annotations and interfaces are compile-time constructs that are stripped during transpilation.

quiz.question: Why should `unknown` be preferred over `any` when handling untrusted or external data?
options: `unknown` disables all type checking
`unknown` requires explicit type checking or narrowing before you can access properties or methods on the value
`unknown` automatically parses JSON
`any` is forbidden in `.tsx` files
quiz.explanation: Unlike `any`, `unknown` preserves type safety by forcing you to narrow the value before using it.

quiz.question: What does the `as const` assertion do on an object literal like `const settings = { theme: 'dark', language: 'en' } as const;`?
options: It converts the object to JSON
It preserves the exact literal types and marks properties as `readonly` instead of widening them to general `string`
It deletes the object at runtime
It makes all properties optional
quiz.explanation: `as const` creates deeply readonly literal types at compile time.

quiz.question: Which statement accurately compares `interface` and `type` aliases in TypeScript?
options: Interfaces can declare union types directly; type aliases cannot
Interfaces support declaration merging and extending object contracts, while type aliases can also represent unions, intersections, primitives, and mapped/conditional types
Type aliases cannot describe objects
Interfaces exist at runtime in the browser
quiz.explanation: Both describe object shapes, with interfaces supporting declaration merging and type aliases supporting unions/primitives/advanced types.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of `readonly` on an interface or type property in TypeScript?
options: It enforces a compile-time restriction preventing reassignment of that property in TypeScript code
It freezes the object deeply in V8 at runtime
It encrypts the property in JSON
It makes the property optional
quiz.explanation: `readonly` is checked at compile time; runtime immutability still requires `Object.freeze()` or immutable updates.

quiz.question: Why do TypeScript generics (`<T>`) improve reusable functions like `getFirstItem<T>(items: T[]): T | undefined`?
options: They erase all type information like `any`
They preserve the caller's specific element type across reusable utilities and components
They convert arrays into tuples automatically
They disable `strictNullChecks`
quiz.explanation: Generics parameterize types so reusable functions, interfaces, and components keep full type safety.

quiz.question: What does `keyof Course` produce for `interface Course { id: number; title: string; duration: number; }`?
options: `"number" | "string"`
`"id" | "title" | "duration"`
`Course[]`
`unknown`
quiz.explanation: `keyof` produces a union of an object type's property keys.

quiz.question: In a discriminated union (`status: 'loading' | 'success' | 'error'`), how does `assertNever(state)` with parameter type `never` help?
options: It suppresses all TypeScript errors
It provides exhaustive checking so TypeScript reports a compile-time error if a new union variant is added without handling it in the `switch`
It retries failed API calls
It converts `null` to `undefined`
quiz.explanation: Exhaustive `never` checks catch unhandled union cases at compile time when states evolve.

quiz.question: What does a user-defined type guard return annotation `value is Student` tell TypeScript?
options: When the function returns `true`, TypeScript narrows the checked variable to `Student` inside that branch
It automatically validates every backend API response without writing checks
It converts a class into an interface
It marks `value` as `any`
quiz.explanation: A type predicate (`value is Student`) informs the compiler that a truthy return value guarantees the narrowed type.

quiz.question: Which file extension is used for TypeScript files that contain React JSX syntax?
options: .ts
.tsx
.jsx
.json
quiz.explanation: `.tsx` is used for TypeScript files containing JSX, whereas `.ts` is used for TypeScript without JSX.
